author: ttfreitas
text:
Ifmyante wrote: Lovely rejection PA today on Gasoline

Hello IF.

Great to see your PA posts again.

I have a few questions if you don't mind.

Despite the display of a lovely rejection PA at supply, price didn't compress to that area (well, at least on the 1min chart).

Did you take the trade, regardless?

If so, are there particular situations when you don't consider compression? What are they?

I can definitely see the trade on the demand side, though, with compression preceding the QM.

Thanks in advance.

author: Ifmyante
text:
This perhaps should be the first thing that anybody ever reads regarding trading:

We're always looking for signs of what the big guys are doing at
significant areas, and if we don't see what they're doing, there's no
trade

So, on approach, if we see the big guys trying to hide their orders in
the market, we see compression, and can feel pretty sure of their
intentions - to get in as many orders as they can before the turn

If we don't see this, we can be pretty sure that it won't just turn
immediately, as there usually won't be enough orders against them to
fill all the orders they must fill.

This is why we wait for an engulf. This shows their intention to reverse
 price. Then we watch them trying to hide their orders in the market on a
 retrace, ready to take price to the origin of the move

text:
Ifmyante wrote: This perhaps should be the first thing that anybody ever reads regarding trading:

fill all the orders they must fill.

This is why we wait for an engulf. This shows their intention to reverse
 price. Then we watch them trying to hide their orders in the market on a
 retrace, ready to take price to the origin of the move

I'll interpret what you said above to ensure I understand it properly, because I believe this is crucial.

I'll use two examples to illustrate my interpretation.

Apologies for polluting your journal.

If price compresses to, let's say, supply, the big guys are already giving away their intentions.

For arguments sake, if compression is perfect (no demand left behind),
then that's the only signal you need. Trade as soon as you get a few
candles rejecting higher highs. YOU DON"T NEED CONFIRMATION (??) (That's my first question) BECAUSE COMPRESSION IS ENOUGH TO DISCLOSE BIG MONEY'S INTENTIONS.

The example below is PA on the EURUSD.

Compression into supply was nearly perfect. Do we wait for the retest
after the engulfing or can we enter as soon as the euro prints the
rejection bar?

(I ask this because if there is no demand left, price will unlikely return for a retest of the break, right?)

When price doesn't compress to, let's say, supply, then we will need
some kind of signal that reveals big money's intentions. The signal is
the engulf.

Then we wait for a retest of left over supply, or break of flag or resistance.

The example below is recent PA in the EURGBP.

IF, is this the correct way to interpret your quote?

Thanks heaps in advance.

text:
